title: The Space Race

cards.h: A beeping ball the size of a beach ball scared America
cards.b:
On 4 October 1957, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, a 58-cm metal sphere. It beeped as it circled Earth. People with radios could hear it.

Americans feared Soviet rockets could now carry bombs. The race to space had begun.
The Soviets sent the dog Laika (November 1957) and then Yuri Gagarin, who orbited Earth for 108 minutes on 12 April 1961.

Weeks later, President Kennedy told Congress the US would land a man on the Moon before the decade ended. In 1962 he said 'we choose to go to the Moon'. Apollo cost the equivalent of well over a hundred billion modern dollars.

In 1967 three astronauts died in the Apollo 1 fire.

Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed Apollo 11's lander on the Moon, while Michael Collins orbited above. Armstrong stepped out first. About 600 million people watched on TV.

Six Apollo missions landed 12 men by 1972. The Soviet Moon rocket, the N1, exploded repeatedly and never worked.

In 1975, an American Apollo and a Soviet Soyuz docked in orbit. Later, the two nations built the International Space Station (from 1998).

Today, private firms and many countries also launch rockets.

cards.h: Was the Moon landing faked? Did NASA spend millions on a pen?
cards.b: Myth 1: it was faked.Fact: evidence includes 382 kg of Moon rock, reflectors left on the surface that scientists still use, and independent tracking by other countries.Myth 2: NASA built a space pen while the Soviets used a pencil. In fact, pencils were used by both, and the Fisher pen was developed privately.

Five things to remember

  1. Sputnik (1957) started the race.
  2. Gagarin was first in space (1961).
  3. Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969.
  4. The rivals later cooperated.
  5. India went from a bicycle to Mars.

Think about it

  • Was the race worth it?
  • What can India's low-cost model teach?
